source: សៀវភៅ 'មធ្យោបាយប្រើប្រាស់ឧបករណ៍ព្រោះជាជួរ' (How to Use the Row/Drum Seeder Tool), presented by an agricultural extension teacher for the Agricultural Productivity Enhancement Project in the West Tonle Sap area (APPP) / CAVAC (Cambodia Agricultural Value Chain program), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries -- Battambang provincial department, 2014
text: Five-step field preparation and seeding sequence for the drum/row seeder: (1) initial plowing of dry or lightly moist soil to break up the field; (2) puddling/wet plowing once the field is flooded, turning the soil into mud; (3) a first harrowing/leveling pass to smooth the puddled soil surface so it is soft and level enough for the seeder; (4) a second harrowing/leveling pass to remove remaining unevenness before sowing, since an uneven field causes uneven water depth and uneven seedling establishment; (5) drum-seeding itself, walking the wheeled, seed-filled drum tool in straight lines across the leveled field so it deposits pre-germinated seed in evenly spaced rows. The source frames land leveling before sowing (steps 3-4) as the step that most determines how uniformly the crop establishes afterward.
